hooks.text: A distant star seems to shine with short-lived radioactive elements.
Why does a billion-year-old star glow with short-lived radioactive waste?
This star shouldn't exist, yet it glows with radioactive promethium.

title: The Star That Glows With Radioactive Waste
description: Przybylski's Star baffled astronomers with signs of short-lived radioactive elements. Decades later, its impossible light remains a cosmic puzzle.

beats.text: A distant star seems to shine with short-lived radioactive elements.
beats.visual: illustration of the starry sky showing the constellation Centaurus

beats.text: We expect stars to be made of hydrogen, with atmospheres containing common metals like iron.
beats.visual: Stellar absorption spectrum showing dark Fraunhofer lines

beats.text: In 1961, astronomer Antoni Przybylski analyzed a star three hundred fifty-six light-years away.
beats.visual: Antoni Przybylski astronomer portrait at Mount Stromlo Observatory

beats.text: Its spectrum showed almost no iron, but was swamped by rare-earth elements thousands of times more abundant than in our Sun.
beats.visual: Periodic table highlighting the Lanthanides and Actinides
queries: Periodic table showing rare earth elements

beats.text: Weirder still, early reports identified promethium, a radioactive element with a half-life of only seventeen point seven years.
queries: Standard periodic table of elements svg

beats.text: In a billion-year-old star, these elements should have decayed away eons ago.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a highly magnetic chemically peculiar star
queries: Magnetic field lines rotating star illustration

beats.text: While physicists hypothesized exotic nuclear decay, 2023 analyses contested the finding due to severe spectral line crowding.
beats.visual: Very Large Telescope at Paranal Observatory under a starry sky
queries: Very Large Telescope Paranal night sky

beats.text: Yet, the longest-lived of these elements decay away in just seventeen point seven years.
beats.visual: artist's concept of the chemically peculiar Przybylski's Star
